title: observability-trace-metrics-log-ingestion-debug-notes-kai-wip
content:
Purpose / context:
- Personal debug scratchpad for the recent telemetry gaps incident (traces + metrics drops + log ingestion delays).
- Working hypothesis: upstream request router started sampling changes -> downstream writer rate-limited -> batch writer panic on malformed proto -> cascading drops. Need to verify end-to-end.

Timeline / breadcrumbs (local notes):
- 2026-02-14 09:10: spike in dropped metrics alerted via pager duty (alert: metrics.ingestion.drop_rate > 5% over 5m).
- 2026-02-14 09:13 observed increased 5xx from telemetry-ingest frontend (svc/telemetry-frontend) in Grafana.
- 2026-02-14 09:20 started tracing hooks validation in staging-like cluster.
- 2026-02-15 10:00 reproduced locally with load generator hitting /v1/telemetry/ingest -> results: 30% traces rejected, 18% metrics dropped, logs delayed 60-90s.

Commands I ran (notes + output snippets):
- kubectl (cluster: prod-obsv-a):
  - kubectl get pods -n observability
    -> telemetry-frontend-56b7c7d8   3/3 Running   3 (3d)
       telemetry-writer-0             0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  restarts: 12
  - kubectl logs telemetry-writer-0 -n observability --since=30m
    + sample output:
    2026-02-14T09:12:21Z ERROR writer: bulk write failed: EOF
    2026-02-14T09:12:21Z WARN  writer: dropped 132 spans (write error)
    2026-02-14T09:12:22Z ERROR writer: failed to decode trace: invalid span format

- curl endpoints (local staging):
  - curl -sS http://localhost:9411/api/v2/traces -X POST --data-binary @sample_trace.json -v
    -> 400 Bad Request on a subset of traces (those including baggage header x-rw-sampled=false)

- prometheus scrape check:
  - curl http://telemetry-writer.svc.cluster.local:9090/metrics | grep ingestion
    -> telemetry_ingestion_write_errors_total  189
       telemetry_ingestion_dropped_spans_total 132

- quick grep in logs for sampler changes:
  - kubectl logs telemetry-frontend-56b7c7d8 -n observability | grep -E "sampler|sampling|sample_rate"
    + output:
    2026-02-14T09:11:55Z INFO sampling: applied new policy from config-service (policy_id=pol-2026-02-14-a)
    2026-02-14T09:11:56Z DEBUG sampling: rule match route=/v1/telemetry/ingest sample_rate=0.05

Error snippets observed (copied verbatim):
- "failed to decode trace: invalid span format"
- "bulk write failed: EOF"
- "rate limiter: exceeded max tokens, dropping 42 metrics"
- "proto: unexpected EOF while reading message"

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Sampling policy change (config-service rollout) reduced sampled traces by 95% for some routes -> downstream writer batches rely on presence of sampling headers and have an edge case where empty batch + malformed header triggers proto decode error. Explains traces missing and some crash loops.
2) Rate limiter misconfigured on telemetry-writer after a recent dependency bump to go-kit/middleware (0.9.2 -> 1.0.0) causing token bucket behavior to be stricter. Explains metrics being dropped but not necessarily trace decode errors.
3) Upstream ingress added an HTTP/2 termination proxy (sidecar config) that strips/rewrites certain headers (x-b3-*, x-rw-sampled) -> malformed proto when writer attempts to rehydrate batched payloads.
4) IO pressure / disk full on writer node causing partial writes and EOFs. (Less likely: node disk usage was 60% during the incident).

Data to gather / experiments to run next:
- Reproduce locally with sample_trace.json variants: include and remove custom sampling headers to see which cause 400 vs accepted.
- Pull telemetry-writer stacktrace for the CrashLoopBackOff pod to get the panic site. kubectl logs -p telemetry-writer-0 -n observability --previous
- Add debug logging around proto decode in writer (instrument to log first 128 bytes of payload when decode fails).
- Temporarily roll back config-service sampling policy to previous config to validate hypothesis #1. (Coordinate with @Zoe).
- Increase writer rate limiter threshold for a 10m window to see if metric drops stop.

Quick tests I ran (results):
- local reproduce: sending 1k traces with sample header x-rw-sampled=false -> ~400 rejected, server returned 400 with body: "invalid sample header: cannot be false for agent-batched payloads"
- sending without sample header -> accepted (200) and writer metrics show increments in ingestion_count.

Notes on linked artifacts / history:
- config-service rollout history: config-service/deployments shows revision 2026-02-14-08:45 (includes sampling policy pol-2026-02-14-a).
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-configs/pull/88 (sampling policy change).
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-482 created by monitoring on 2026-02-14 09:15.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Add guard in writer: reject empty batches earlier and emit metric telemetry_writer_empty_batches_total (low overhead).
- [ ] Instrument decode failure payload snapshot (first N bytes) behind a prod-only flag.
- [ ] Coordinate rollback test for sampling policy with ConfigSRE (Zoe).
- [ ] Patch go-kit/bucket middleware in telemetry-writer to increase burst window and monitor for 1 hour.
- [ ] Follow up: if rollback fixes, schedule a safer rollout with canary + sampling test harness.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did only certain traces trigger the "invalid span format"? (Look at fields that differ: baggage headers, compressed payloads?)
- Is there any difference in route-level behavior between hosted-api traffic and internal telemetry (are we applying the same sampling rules)?
- Did any infrastructure change (kube-proxy, envoy sidecar config) happen around 2026-02-14 08:40-09:00? Check infra-change-log.

Notes-to-self (quick TODO commands):
- reproduce: python tools/load_test.py --endpoint http://localhost:8080/v1/telemetry/ingest --payload samples/sample_trace_with_baggage.json --rps 200 --duration 300
- fetch previous writer logs: kubectl logs telemetry-writer-0 -n observability --tail=500 > /tmp/writer-logs.txt
- run binary with debug: make build && docker run -e LOG_LEVEL=debug telemetry-writer:local

If I can't resolve today: escalate to eng-sre oncall (pager duty) + mark as Sev2. Current plan: rollback sampling policy -> monitor 30m -> if errors drop, mark root cause = mis-rolled sampling config; otherwise collect payload samples and escalate.

End of note (will keep appending).

Last quick copy of interesting log block:
2026-02-14T09:12:20Z INFO  batching: new batch id=bb-20260214-1101 size=24
2026-02-14T09:12:21Z ERROR writer: bulk write failed: EOF
2026-02-14T09:12:21Z WARN  writer: dropped 132 spans (write error)
2026-02-14T09:12:22Z ERROR writer: failed to decode trace: invalid span format: proto: unexpected EOF
2026-02-14T09:12:22Z DEBUG sampling: route=/v1/telemetry/ingest sampled=false header=x-rw-sampled=false
